TLR8 receptor on NK cells could play important role in development of RSV-specific adaptive immune response and in control of RSV infection severity in infants.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lower TLR 8 expression in NK-cells of RSV-infected children is related to impaired IFN-γ response and could be associated with severity of RSV infection.
RSV-infected infant NK cells have decreased TLR8 expression and IFN-γ response that could be related to severity of infection.
TLR8 receptor is involved in RSV pathogenesis in infants and its expression is related to the severity of disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TLR8 expression on NK cells in RSV-infected infant is lower in comparison to healthy infants and adults, and is associated with severity of infection and IFN-γ levels.
TLR8 is an important receptor in NK cells, which is downregulated during RSV infection in infants and this could be a mechanism of RSV pathogenesis in infants.
TLR8 expression levels on NK cells could be used as a marker to monitor the severity of RSV infections in infants.
